prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title 'Five domains to observe'. Five large evenly spaced wooden alphabet blocks spell F L A C C across the page. Under F a simple round wooden face token with neutral cartoon eyes and mouth, label 'Face'. Under L a pair of empty toy trousers with two legs, label 'Legs'. Under A a small rocking horse with motion marks, label 'Activity'. Under first C a sound-ripple symbol, label 'Cry'. Under last C two teddy bears leaning together for comfort, label 'Consolability'. Short prominent phrase 'Observe behaviour'. Bottom note 'Domain reminder; use the validated scoring tool'. Five icons visually distinct and entirely original; NO standard faces pain scale, scores, numeric ranges or copied rubric descriptors. No anatomy or photorealistic child.

teaching.question: Which five behavioural observations make up FLACC?
teaching.answer: Face, Legs, Activity, Cry and Consolability. Each is observed using the validated scoring tool; this mnemonic alone is not a scoring form.

title: Five domains to observe
caption: FLACC combines observations of face, legs, activity, cry and consolability. This original mnemonic illustrates the domains; it does not reproduce or replace the validated scoring form.
alt: Five letter tiles F L A C C pair with generic face, trouser legs, moving toy, sound ripple and comfort icons.

review.notes: Verified F-L-A-C-C order and Face/Legs/Activity/Cry/Consolability mapping. Each object serves the intended behavioural mnemonic. No copied faces scale, scoring table, patient score or internal anatomy. The validated-scoring-tool note makes the mnemonic boundary clear.
